name: Mengaka
world_status: a description exists but is not accessible

sources.citation: Rovenchak, Andrij. 2009. Towards the decipherment of the Bagam script. Afrikanistik-Aegyptologie-Online 2009. doi:10.18716/ojs/aaeo/2009_3537
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: No rule. Para <10> only explains Malcolm's 1920s transcription conventions for Eghap words ('The macron marks stress, the caron does unstress, and accent is marked by the acute'); nothing on where stress falls.

sources.citation: Anderson, Stephen C. 2001. Phonological characteristics of Eastern Grassfields languages. In Mutaka & Chumbow (eds.), Research Mate in African Linguistics: Focus on Cameroon (GAAS 17), 33-54. Koeln: Koeppe. (archive.org scanned text layer, held under bafu1246)
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request); access check: held in print at Harvard (Widener Library (offsite storage), call number PL8021.C35 R47 2001); the library holds the journal volume but the item itself was not found; ask your own library for a scan or interlibrary loan
sources.harvard_location: Widener Library (offsite storage), call number PL8021.C35 R47 2001
sources.note: Family-level claim, sec. 6 p. 47: in Eastern Grassfields nouns and verbs 'the first syllable of the root is stressed'; prefixes and second root syllables unstressed. Examples from Ngiemboon; Bamileke subgroup listed p. 33 ('Fe'fe', Ghomala', Yemba, Ngwe, Ngiemboon, Ngomba, Ngombale, etc.'), Mengaka not named.

sources.citation: OLAC listing for xmg (Internet Archive copy 2024-12-24 of language-archives.org/language/xmg): only Seguin 1993, Ethnologue, Glottolog, LINGUIST List, Rosetta Project Genesis portion.
sources.note: Confirms no other language description is catalogued.

sources.citation: Seguin, Lawrence Marc. 1993. A rapid appraisal survey of Mengaka (ALCAM 930), Bamboutos Division, West Province. Yaounde: SIL / Ministry of Scientific and Technical Research. 12 pp. (SIL archives 47675). downloaded via web.archive.org from sil.org reapdata URL; image scan, scanned at 300 dpi.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Nothing. Sociolinguistic rapid appraisal only; p. 1 states 'no evidence was found of prior linguistic studies or standardisation efforts in Mengaka'. No tone/stress/accent remarks.

sources.citation: Tuchscherer, Konrad. 1999. The Lost Script of the Bagam. African Affairs 98(390): 55-77.
sources.tag: likely states stress; not yet obtained
sources.access_detail: a digital copy exists, paywalled at the publisher (DOI); library e-access not checked
sources.note: Reproduces Malcolm's 1917-21 Eghap transcriptions with stress/accent diacritics; not a rule statement but the only published Mengaka data with marked stress.

sources.citation: Feussi, Valentin. 1991. Esquisse phonologique du megaka (parler du Bagam). Memoire de maitrise, Universite de Yaounde I. 130 pp.
sources.tag: likely states stress; not yet obtained
sources.access_detail: open link recorded by Glottolog or the catalog, not checked; access check: not located online or in the libraries checked
sources.note: The only phonological description of Mengaka known to Glottolog (Glottolog's most extensive description = phonology); a Yaounde structuralist sketch of this series normally has a 'tons'/'accent' section that would settle whether any word-accent statement exists. Hammarstrom holds a scan not deposited on MPG PuRe.

sources.note: Comparative overview of Mbam-Nkam including Bagam/Mengaka data from the Grassfields Bantu Working Group; may contain general prosodic remarks (tone/stem prominence) covering Bamileke lects.
